title: Introduction to Middlewares
summary: Explains what Express middleware is (code that runs on every request before the route handlers), recaps HTML form attributes, shows how to serve a file with res.sendFile and a computed __dirname, and wires up body-parser so form data appears on req.body.

concepts.heading: What middleware is and what it is used for
points: Middleware is a function that sits between the incoming request and the route handlers (app.get, app.post, app.put and so on). It can inspect or change the request before a handler sees it.

Typical jobs: pre-processing requests shared by several handlers, logging (method, timing, status), authentication/authorisation checks before the request reaches back-end logic, and detecting or handling errors early.
Registered with app.use(...) above the routes, so it runs first for every matching request.

concepts.heading: HTML form recap (needed for the exercise)
points: <form action="/submit" method="POST">: action is the route on the server that receives the data; method is the HTTP verb used (POST here, since the form sends data to the server).
<label> describes the input that follows it; the for attribute links it to an input by id.
<input type="text" name="street">: type picks the control (text, radio, checkbox, submit, etc.); name is the key under which the typed value is sent, producing key/value pairs.
required blocks submission until the field is filled in.
<input type="submit" value="Submit"> renders the button; value is the button's label.
Submitting a form like this sends an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body, e.g. street=Aberdeen&pet=rabbit.

concepts.heading: Serving a file with res.sendFile and computing __dirname
points: Static files (HTML, CSS, images) live in a public folder. Instead of res.send(string), use res.sendFile(absolutePath) to return a whole file.
sendFile needs an absolute path. Hard-coding one breaks once the server is hosted elsewhere, so compute it at runtime.
In ES modules there is no built-in __dirname. Rebuild it: import { dirname } from 'path'; import { fileURLToPath } from 'url'; const __dirname = dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
import.meta.url is the file URL of the current module; fileURLToPath turns it into a normal OS path; dirname strips the file name, leaving the folder.
Then: res.sendFile(__dirname + '/public/index.html'). The path adapts to Mac, Windows, Linux or a cloud host.
(Extra) Newer Node versions also offer import.meta.dirname, and Express supports res.sendFile(path, { root: ... }) as another way to avoid string concatenation.

concepts.heading: body-parser middleware
points: Install with npm i body-parser (already in the starter package.json, but needed when building from scratch), then import bodyParser from 'body-parser'.

Add it with app.use(bodyParser.urlencoded({ extended: true })). urlencoded selects the parser for HTML form data. The extended option is required; it chooses which library parses the string behind the scenes (true = qs, supports nested objects; false = querystring). Using true is the near-universal choice.
The effect: every request gains a body property. Without the middleware req.body is undefined.

Put the logic in a POST handler, not GET: app.post('/submit', (req, res) => { console.log(req.body); }). GET only returns resources; POST receives data. The path must match the form action exactly, including case.
(Extra) The sample handler never responds, so the browser keeps loading. Add res.send(...) or res.sendStatus(200) to finish the request.
(Extra) Express 4.16+ includes express.urlencoded() built in, which does the same job; the reference solution1.js uses it.

concepts.heading: Testing with Postman and the browser
points: Run with nodemon index1.js (the folder has index1-4 files, one per sub-exercise).
In Postman: method POST, URL localhost:3000/submit, Body tab, x-www-form-urlencoded, add any key/value pairs, Send. The console prints them as an object.
Removing the body-parser line and sending again prints undefined, proving the middleware is what creates req.body.
In the browser, open localhost:3000, fill the Band Name Generator form (street name and pet name), submit, and the terminal shows { street: ..., pet: ... }.

task.name: 3.4 Middleware, index1.js: log submitted form data
task.starting_point: Download the exercise zip, extract, cd into it, run npm install. index1.js already has the express, path/url and body-parser imports plus __dirname and a GET route that sends public/index.html; the POST route is missing or incomplete.
task.goal: Submitting the Band Name Generator form should print the entered street and pet values in the terminal via req.body.
steps: Open the project folder, run npm install, and start with nodemon index1.js.
Install body-parser (npm i body-parser) if not already in dependencies and import it.
Register app.use(bodyParser.urlencoded({ extended: true })) before the routes.
Add app.post('/submit', ...) whose handler console.logs req.body.
Open localhost:3000, fill both fields, press Submit, and check the terminal output.
Optionally comment out the app.use line to confirm req.body becomes undefined.
task.expected_result: Terminal shows an object such as { street: 'Aberdeen', pet: 'rabbit' } after each submit.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 24 - Express.js with Node.js/24.04 - Introduction to Middlewares/solution1.js

pitfalls: Registering app.use(bodyParser...) after the routes, so req.body is undefined in handlers.
Form action and app.post path differing in spelling or case.
Missing name attributes on inputs, so no keys appear in req.body.
Forgetting to extract the zip or run npm install in the right folder.
Handler never sends a response, so the browser hangs.
Reference repo note: public/index.html contains a personal footer from the repo author; ignore it.
